definitions.explanation: Fruit that has had most of its moisture removed through drying, producing a shelf-stable product with concentrated flavor and sweetness. Includes raisins, dried apricots, dried figs, dried mangoes, and the like.

examples.japanese: {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}を{食|た}べる。
このパンには{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}が{入|はい}っています。
{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}は{糖分|とうぶん}が{多|おお}いので{食|た}べすぎに{注意|ちゅうい}しましょう。
examples.english: Dried fruit is high in sugar, so be careful not to eat too much.

examples.japanese: {朝食|ちょうしょく}のヨーグルトに{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}とナッツを{加|くわ}えると、{栄養|えいよう}バランスがよくなる。
examples.english: Adding dried fruit and nuts to your breakfast yogurt improves the nutritional balance.

notes:
Composed of {乾燥|かんそう} (drying, dehydration) and {果実|かじつ} (fruit). The scientific or formal term for dried fruit.

REGISTER:
{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ} is the precise, technical term seen on food packaging, in nutrition articles, ingredient lists, and recipes. In casual speech and everyday shopping, the loanword {ドライフルーツ|どらいふるーつ} is far more common. Both refer to the same thing, but {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ} sounds more scientific or formal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}{入|い}り: containing dried fruit
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}を{加|くわ}える: to add dried fruit
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}{加工|かこう}: dried-fruit processing
- {無添加|むてんか}の{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}: additive-free dried fruit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ドライフルーツ: dried fruit — the everyday loanword, far more common in conversation
- {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}: dried fruit — a more native-sounding synonym
- {干|ほ}しぶどう: raisins — a specific type of dried fruit
- {生|なま}{果実|かじつ}: fresh fruit — the opposite; unprocessed fresh fruit
